images.title: Fewest for HCF, most for LCM
images.purpose: Sum up the chapter: from prime factorisations, the HCF takes the fewest of each prime and the LCM the most, linked back to the 12 ft by 16 ft tile room.
images.composition: Two factorisation lines at top centre, two arrows down to an HCF box at left and an LCM box at right, and a small tiled room under the HCF box, wide white space.
exact_structure: Top centre: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 and, beneath it, 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Every 2 in teal #0072B2, every 3 in amber #E69F00.
Two grey #6B7280 arrows down, one to the left and one to the right.
Left box, reddish purple #CC79A7 outline: HCF: fewest of each prime, then 2 × 2 = 4.
Right box, green #009E73 outline: LCM: most of each prime, then 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 48.
Under the HCF box: a small rectangle 3 tiles by 4 tiles, exactly 12 equal square tiles in a light reddish purple, with the caption 4 ft tiles.
rejection: an HCF other than 4 or an LCM other than 48
the tile grid with other than 3 by 4, that is 12, tiles
the words fewest and most swapped between the boxes
images.takeaway: The HCF uses the fewest of each prime and the LCM the most, straight from the prime factorisations.
images.description: 12 and 16 as primes, arrows to HCF 2 × 2 = 4 with a 3 by 4 grid of 4 ft tiles, and LCM 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 48.
images.context: Shown beside the chapter summary text and recap video.
images.teaching_notes: Trace each arrow and say which count of each prime goes into each box.

image_decisions.why: One picture tying prime factorisation to both HCF and LCM is the core of the summary.
